actors: The licensed firm responsible for the assessed STR submission, classified separately under the circular's definition.
The JFIU, which receives the STR and provides the separately referenced technical requirements and resubmission guidance.
Hongkong Post, identified by the source as the provider of the required e-Cert.
objects: One actual submission event for that STR, with its own submitting firm, recipient, channel and timestamp.
The XML representation, uploaded PDF form or STREAMS 2 web-based form used in that event.
For a PDF submission, the prescribed form and its completion state, assessed separately from the act of uploading it.
A Hongkong Post e-Cert, distinguished from both firm-level certificate possession and any act involving the certificate in the assessed submission.
Evidence linking the certificate to the particular XML or PDF submission.
Separate contact, resubmission and record-migration events concerning the same STR.
relationships: The classified licensed firm submits the identified STR to the JFIU through a particular channel at a particular time.
The reporting channel is distinct from the representation or form used: XML or PDF format alone does not establish submission through STREAMS 2.
The PDF alternative requires an upload, use of the prescribed PDF format and a completed STR form; these are separate factual components.
Footnote 3 attaches to the XML and PDF alternatives and describes the e-Cert as required for the submission.
Possession, availability and operational use of a certificate are different relationships. The retained source does not specify which operational act establishes satisfaction of footnote 3.
The web-based alternative has no footnote 3 marker in the retained source.
Direct contact during the blackout is distinct from an actual STR submission; neither is established solely by the other.
A post-implementation submission outside STREAMS 2 and a subsequent STREAMS 2 resubmission are separate events linked by STR identity.
Automatic migration of a previously submitted STREAMS record is distinct from a firm's submission or resubmission event.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One actual STR submission event by one classified licensed firm to the JFIU. Evidence about another submission, another STR or firm-level certificate possession cannot substitute for evidence about this event. A later resubmission is assessed separately.
proposals.temporal_basis: For the ordinary channel and method assessment, interpret the specific launch at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 as the start of the post-launch period. Exclude the blackout beginning at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ending at that launch, including the pre-launch portion of 2 February. The governing timezone remains to be established. Assess certificate-related evidence for the particular submission; the source does not specify a certificate validity interval or operational verification time.
classification_assumptions: The filing entity's membership in the circular's licensed-firm categories requires a separate assessment and is not inferred from platform use.
The specific launch and resumption provisions qualify the general effective-date wording for the post-launch assessment.
The selected event is an actual STR submission to the JFIU; registration, a technical test, direct contact and automatic record migration are separate event classifications.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method. Evidence from separate attempts or resubmissions is not combined to make one event satisfy the selected conditions.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and prescribed-PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No certificate requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.

The source establishes a submission-related e-Cert requirement but does not establish that certificate availability alone satisfies it. Signing, authentication, attachment, certificate-holder identity and validity mechanics are not assumed.

The proposed decision concerns only the selected reporting channel, listed method and footnote 3 condition. It does not establish XML-schema conformity, completion of technical testing, reporting timeliness, substantive STR adequacy or overall legal compliance.

The blackout urgent-contact instruction and footnote 2 resubmission requirement remain separate. Resubmission does not change the original event's channel or time, and the retained text supplies no resubmission deadline.

reading.subject: Submission-specific e-Cert requirement without substituting availability or an undefined satisfaction predicate
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] The proposed question is whether one in-scope post-launch STR submission satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 conditions. True would mean that the event used STREAMS 2 and completed one listed method, including the submission-related Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement where XML or PDF was used. False would mean that at least one applicable selected condition failed. Neither an unknown fact nor an unknown or false scope produces a compliance verdict. Formalization is null because the retained source does not specify the certificate relationship needed to interpret the XML and PDF branches without substituting an unsupported operational assumption or an opaque satisfaction fact. No event-level truth value is assigned. This proposed meaning confers no legal approval.
reading.distinction: The prior models already identify the relevant actors, distinguish channel from method, preserve the launch boundary and separate submission, contact, migration and resubmission events. The consequential remaining defect is the certificate relationship. Model abstraction.c8a341a59885fb7db63017bf makes certificate availability sufficient under an explicit assumption. Model abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9 instead requires supply or use 'in the manner required', but the required manner remains unspecified. The retained footnote supports a requirement for the particular submission; it does not resolve availability versus the operational act needed to satisfy that requirement. This proposal therefore withholds a complete compliance formula pending that information. It does not invent a rival signing, attachment or authentication requirement. Splitting the PDF components also prevents the file's format from concealing an incomplete form or a missing upload.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued. All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2.

licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.

unresolved: One proposal is sufficient for this challenge: the supplied prior models already preserve the principal actor, event, report-history and timing distinctions. No additional rival actor or certificate mechanism is established by the retained source.

The certificate-availability assumption in abstraction.c8a341a59885fb7db63017bf remains an assumption, not a source-established satisfaction test. The required-manner predicate in abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9 remains unresolved until its operational meaning can be stated without incorporating the legal conclusion into an input fact.

The original-event trigger in abstraction.42a1f989e579c54a02f14a58 and the report-history trigger in abstraction.f80753837baaf4d0166ecbca answer different questions. A false trigger for one selected event does not establish that no other qualifying submission of the same STR exists. A report-level false result requires sufficient event-history evidence; neither trigger establishes discharge or lateness.

The blackout instruction remains applicable to STRs requiring urgent submission during that interval and calls for direct JFIU contact by a listed method. Its satisfaction is not evaluated by this proposal. Contact alone does not establish filing, and the source does not expressly extend footnote 2 to blackout-only submissions.

The separately supplied XML schema and technical-test arrangements may add requirements beyond the selected channel, method and certificate conditions. Intention to use XML is a firm-level condition distinct from a completed XML submission event; the prior event models do not evaluate that preparatory instruction.

The four listed missing dependencies have no supplied contents or source hashes. Their requirements, if any, remain unexamined. The retained evidence does not establish legal completeness or release eligibility.
